point: Wadi Qumran bed below Kh. Qumran
record_basis: atlas-data.json places/wadi_qumran (31.74111, 35.45056; Wikidata Q7218539) and places/kh_qumran (31.74183, 35.45941); ratings.csv entry 20 candidate wadi_qumran
how_fixed: D8 channel traced from the wadi_qumran atlas point; the bed cell nearest the kh_qumran atlas point (287 m SW of it), just below the gorge waterfall (DEM step -253 to -359 m within 230 m)
why_chosen_or_note: 'Below Kh. Qumran' read as the bed beside and below the settlement, where the gorge opens onto the shore terrace. The atlas wadi_qumran point itself snaps to the gorge above the waterfall (31.74094, 35.45365, z -246); kept as an alternative.

point: el-Buqeia plateau wadi bed (Nahal Sekhakha / Wadi Qumran headwaters)
record_basis: atlas-data.json places/buqeia (31.7177, 35.3948; PEF XVIII label point Kh. es-Sumrah, 'area ~5 km'); ratings.csv entry 17 candidate buqeia; run 7 (samra_hyrcania_valley) RESULT: Nahal Sekhakha is a Wadi Qumran tributary
how_fixed: largest drainage-area cell within 400 m of the atlas label point (396 m NNE)
why_chosen_or_note: The atlas point is only a label anchor at Kh. es-Samra; the nearest plateau channel is used. Any plateau bed within c. 5 km is equally eligible under the record; the plateau's own fill regime applies, not the gorge's.

point: Wadi Nuweimeh bed NE of Jericho
record_basis: atlas-data.json places/nuweimeh (31.8837, 35.4409; PEF XVIII lower-course label 'Wady en Nueiameh', area ~3 km); ratings.csv entry 17 candidate nuweimeh
how_fixed: largest drainage-area cell within 400 m of the label point (400 m ESE)
why_chosen_or_note: Lower course on the Jericho plain/fan, as the label. The candidate is a 3 km area; the point stands for the lower course only.

point: Kidron (Wadi en-Nar) bed at Deir Mar Saba
record_basis: atlas-data.json places/mar_saba (31.70494, 35.33115; Pleiades 687969); ratings.csv entry 35 candidate mar_saba; run 4/route anchors.csv same point
how_fixed: largest drainage-area cell within 400 m of the Pleiades monastery point (387 m SSE), on the gorge floor
why_chosen_or_note: Gorge floor below the monastery. The record's cairns (Mar Saba map Sites 99, 100, 108) lie c. 0.9 km downstream; same reach.

point: Kidron exit to the Dead Sea shore (fan apex at the foot of the fault escarpment)
record_basis: ratings.csv entry 35 U_basis (rival stretch: the Kidron where it leaves the escarpment, Dahari; Q34); atlas mar_saba note ('The escarpment exit remains another possibility'); Kh. Mazin record point 31.68219, 35.44221 (ADAJ 6/7 1962 pp. 96-103; HA-ESI 136 2024) c. 1 km ENE
how_fixed: D8 trace of the Kidron from P4a: the bed drops from -128 m to -364 m between 13.1 and 13.7 km below Mar Saba (the fault scarp); the first cell below the drop is taken as the exit / fan apex
why_chosen_or_note: The rule names the exit to the Dead Sea shore. No project record pins the gorge mouth; the canyon-exit cell on the DEM is used. The fan surface runs from here to the -412 m DEM shore c. 2.5 km E.

point: Wadi el-Qelt bed at Choziba (St George's monastery)
record_basis: atlas-data.json places/choziba (31.84408, 35.41178; Pleiades 687876); ratings.csv entry 32 candidate choziba
how_fixed: largest drainage-area cell within 300 m of the Pleiades point (293 m NE)
why_chosen_or_note: Gorge floor below the monastery. DEM (c. 16 m cells, SRTM-derived) smooths the narrow gorge, so the bed elevation is approximate.

record_basis: atlas-data.json places/kuteif (31.802, 35.411; PEF XVIII 'Wady Ekteif' label, area ~3 km); ratings.csv entry 24 candidate kuteif
how_fixed: largest drainage-area cell within 500 m of the label point (494 m SE)
why_chosen_or_note: The undated stepped chamber (SWP III p. 220; Milik D12) has no coordinate in the record; the label point stands for the wadi.

point: Lower Jordan channel / floodplain near Jericho at the Qasr el-Yahud crossing
record_basis: atlas-data.json places/jordan_ford has no coordinates ('no ford identified', label only on the river east of Jericho); research/regional/water_systems/water.csv rows LIT-HIR-QASRYAHUD (31.837987, 35.538737; WBADB S2651 Qasr el-Yahud); research/history/pef_qs_finds search_terms 'jordan_ford' lists Hajlah, Ghoraniyeh, Qasr el-Yahud
how_fixed: lowest DEM cell on an E-W transect at the latitude of the Qasr el-Yahud record point (840 m E of it)
why_chosen_or_note: No ford is identified in the project. The Qasr el-Yahud crossing is the only lower-Jordan crossing with a coordinate in the project's records near Jericho, so it is used as the representative point. Other fords (SWP p. 170: Hajlah, Ghoraniyeh etc.) are not separately placed.

point: Wadi el-Asla / Mukellik (Nahal Og) bed at the escarpment exit nearest the Jofet el-Asla label
record_basis: atlas-data.json places/asla (31.7716, 35.451; PEF XVIII hill label 'Jofet el Asla'; the wadi is not labelled); ratings.csv entry 18 P_basis (Milik: middle part of the Mukellik-Asla-Daber torrent; Clermont-Ganneau: a separate little Wady el-Asala; Q23)
how_fixed: the only channel >5 km2 within 1.5 km of the label point; D8 upstream trace follows it west into the Mukellik system; cell 1.5 km NNE of the label, below the scarp
why_chosen_or_note: Milik's branch (main torrent). Clermont-Ganneau's branch (a small separate wadi) would be a small channel such as 31.77612, 35.45897 (1.5 km2, 0.9 km E of the label); recorded as P8-alt, not scored separately because the rule fixes one position. Uncertainty set to 1.5 km.

point: Kh. Mazin (Qasr el-Yahudi) on the Kidron fan
dem_bed_elev_m: c. -390 to -400 (site; DEM shore cell -412 nearby)
record_basis: project records: research/regional/haesi_features/phase4_2026-10-11/part_i_adaj/features.csv (ADAJ 6/7 1962 pp. 96-103, Stutchbury and Nicholl: a feature 'above the original floor level, below later gravels'); HA-ESI 136 (2024) Kh. Mazin, Traubman, salvage; HA 40 (1971) Bar-Adon: large fort at the outlet of wadis Mazin and en-Nar, Iron II and Hasmonean sherds
why_chosen_or_note: Chosen before reading any sediment source because (1) the project already records later gravels over an original floor at a dated Hasmonean (Second Temple) structure built on a wadi fan; (2) it lies on the same fan as P4b (c. 1 km), so it tests the rates used there; (3) it is near the 1st-c. shore, so it also tests the base-level argument. Needed from step 2: a published section with gravel thickness over the dated floor.

point: Hasmonean and Herodian palaces at Tulul Abu el-Alayiq (Wadi Qelt at the Jericho fan)
record_basis: project records: research/assessments/entry29_jericho_pools (Netzer 1983/1989/2001; Netzer 2006) inventory of the Jericho palace pools; ratings.csv entry 32 (Qelt system, Eshel pp. 97-100)
how_fixed: record point: water.csv / entry29 inventory rows LIT-NET01-FIRSTPOOLS etc. (ASI 109/5/14 Tell el-Alayiq, 31.850423, 35.436225, precision 300 m); HA 59-60 (1976) expedition map ref OIG 1905/1400 (31.85266, 35.42679) is the expedition reference point, c. 900 m W
why_chosen_or_note: Chosen before reading any sediment source because it is the best-excavated dated (Hasmonean to Herodian) complex on a Dead Sea tributary channel, with published sections (Netzer's final reports), on the same wadi as P5 (Wadi Qelt, c. 3 km downstream of Choziba), so it tests the rates used for P5 and the Jericho fan points (P3, P6). Needed from step 2: a published section showing alluvium over or wadi erosion of a dated surface.

point: In order, used only if C1 or C2 has no published section giving a burial depth: (a) Ein Feshkha farm (de Vaux; Hirschfeld 2004), (b) Ein Gedi Roman-Byzantine village on the Nahal David/Arugot fans, (c) Ein Boqeq Herodian officina (Fischer, Gichon and Tal 2000)
how_fixed: Same criteria. Not chosen as primaries because the project has no record of alluvial burial at them.
